paper.title: Bandit Online Learning with Unknown Delays

settings.definition_quote: In delayed MAB, the learner still chooses an arm a_t ~ p_t at the beginning of slot t. However, the loss l_t(a_t) is observed after d_t slots ... we assume that {d_t} can be chosen adversarially by nature ... we consider the case where the delay d_t is not accessible, i.e., the learner just observes the value of l_{s|t}(a_{s|t}), but not s.

unmapped: delays are unknown to the learner (feedback not tagged with its originating round)

settings.definition_quote: \textbf{BCO with unknown delays.} For delayed BCO, the learner still chooses $\bm{x}_t$ to play while querying $\{\bm{x}_{t,k}\}_{k=1}^{M-1}$ at the beginning of slot $t$. However, the loss as well as the querying responses $\big{\{}f_t(\bm{x}_{t,k}) \big{\}}_{k=0}^{M-1}$ are observed at the end of slot $t+d_t$. Similarly, let $f_{s|t}(\bm{x}_{s|t})$ denote the loss incurred in slot $s$ but observed at $t$, and the feedback set at the end of slot $t$ is ${\cal L}_t = \big\{ \{f_{s|t}(\bm{x}_{s|t,k})\}_{k=0}^{M-1}, s:\! s\!+\!d_s \! = \! t \big\}$.

source.label: theo.reg
source.quote: Supposing Assumptions 1 and 2 hold, defining the overall delay $D := \sum_{t=1}^T d_t$, and choosing $\delta_2 = \frac{1}{T+D}$, $\eta = {\cal O} \Big( \sqrt{ \frac{1+\ln K}{\bar{d}K(T+D)} } \Big)$, and $\delta_1 = \frac{1}{2\eta\bar{d}} - \frac{\delta_2}{\eta}$, DEXP3 guarantees that the ${\rm Reg}_T^{\rm MAB}$ in (1) satisfies ${\rm Reg}_T^{\rm MAB} = {\cal O} \big( \sqrt{ (T+D) \bar{d}K (1+\ln K)} \big)$.

results.notes: Regret is the expected loss of p_t minus the loss of the best fixed p* in hindsight. Whether the adversary is oblivious or adaptive is not stated.

conditions: feasible set contains epsilon*unit ball and has diameter R
learner queries d+1 points per round (x_t and x_t + delta e_k)

source.label: theo.reg2
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions 3 - 5 hold. Choosing $\delta= {\cal O}\big((T+D)^{-1}\big)$, and $\eta = {\cal O}\big((T+D)^{-1/2}\big)$, the DBGD guarantees that the regret is bounded, that is ${\rm Reg}_T^{{\rm BCO}} = \sum_{t=1}^T f_t(\bm{x}_t) - \sum_{t=1}^Tf_t(\bm{x}^*) = {\cal O} \big( \sqrt{T+D} \big)$ where $D:= \sum_{t=1}^T d_t$ is the overall delay.

results.notes: The theorem hides the dimension (paper's K = d). The abstract and the proof (with eta = 1/sqrt(K(T+D))) give O(sqrt(K(T+D))). The algorithm is deterministic.

conditions: feasible set contains epsilon*unit ball and has diameter R

source.label: coro.reg
source.quote: Upon defining $\bm{x}_{t,0}:= \bm{x}_t$ and $\bm{x}_{t,k}: =\bm{x}_t+\delta \bm{e}_k$, choosing $\delta= {\cal O}\big((T+D)^{-1}\big)$, and $\eta = {\cal O}\big((T+D)^{-1/2}\big)$, the DBGD also guarantees that $\frac{1}{K+1}\sum_{t=1}^T\sum_{k=0}^{K} f_t(\bm{x}_{t,k}) - \sum_{t=1}^T f_t(\bm{x}^*) = {\cal O}\big( \sqrt{T+D} \big)$.

results.notes: Regret here is the loss averaged over all d+1 query points per round (the Agarwal et al. 2010 definition). The algorithm is deterministic.
